items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: listening to how he transcended anything having to do with just the normal change that was being played

ctx.x: And Joey started giving me theory lessons and the Mehegan Book and started to say well this is what you found out. This is sort of what that is and this is what the substitute changes represent from your theory. And so we started going through that thing. I’d never really followed that through real far, I think I studied with him for about six months. But the idea was that my head opened up to a new process and that was that I never had to just blatantly play what was in front of my face. Because that truly is…

play a B triad in the right hand and just, you know, E and B flat down here. And what happens is when you do this there is the D change to play on, there’s the C7 to play on, but because there’s no root, you’ve got multiple changes to play on from the left hand and you’ve got multiple changes to play on because you’ve got a new key here, you’ve got the left hand key which is not giving you the key of C so you’ve got a whole bunch you can play on there. All of a sudden I’m listening to this and saying —…
